# Cline (VS Code extension, Desktop and CLI)

This host keeps its config in your user profile.

## Install

```
headwaters install --host cline
```

The installer prints the diff first and writes only after a yes; `--dry-run` stops at the
diff and `--json` prints the same plan as a document.

## Files

| File | What the install does |
| --- | --- |
| `<home>/.cline/data/settings/cline_mcp_settings.json` | create |
| `<project>/.clinerules/headwaters.md` | create |
| `<project>/.cline/workflows/headwaters-auto.md` | create |
| `<project>/.cline/workflows/headwaters-free.md` | create |
| `<project>/.cline/workflows/headwaters-handoff.md` | create |
| `<project>/.cline/workflows/headwaters-local.md` | create |
| `<project>/.cline/workflows/headwaters-status.md` | create |

## What you still do

- MCP servers live in your Cline settings (<home>/.cline/data/settings/cline_mcp_settings.json); restart the extension or the CLI task after the install so it reloads them.
- The workflows appear in the slash-command list: type / and pick headwaters-<name>.
- Cline reads .clinerules/ and AGENTS.md: both are kept, so a project that already has one is unchanged.

## Templates behind this page

The entries above are rendered from `cline_mcp` in `headwaters/installer/templates/`, so this page and a real install cannot drift.

## Check it

```
headwaters doctor --host cline
```

The doctor reads this host's own config back and reports a missing or stale entry; a
clean report means the host is talking to the gateway.

## Remove it

```
headwaters uninstall --host cline
```

The uninstall restores the backed-up file unless it was edited after the install; then it
asks for `--force`.
